transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Newcrest CTO), Priya Patel (VP Eng), Diego Ramos (Infra Lead), Sofia Li (Procurement)

Summary: quick check-in ahead of renewal to discuss capacity increase (reserved GPUs), adding EU and AP regions, and contract length options. Agreed to run sandbox perf tests and circulate updated commercial terms.

Topics: capacity upgrades, additional regions, contract extension (12 vs 18 months), SOC2/ISO evidence, VPC/private deployment options, latency vs cost tradeoffs.

Action items (auto): see action items section below.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm joined by Maya. How are you all?
[00:00:10] Liam: Hey Jordan, good thanks. Busy week but good to sync.
[00:00:15] Priya: Hi all. We just want to make sure we lock down capacity and regions before the renewal.
[00:00:22] Jordan: Totally. Quick agenda — we want to review current usage, talk about your requested capacity bump, region add-ons, and then commercial term options. Maya will cover the perf plan.
[00:00:30] Maya: Hi — glad to be here. Diego, can you remind us your current p95 latency and token throughput numbers?
[00:00:37] Diego: Yeah, roughly p95 for our gen workloads is about 220ms for short chat flows in us-east-1, throughput peaks around 1200 tokens/sec across bursts. The big pain is when we hit peak retail hours we see queueing and some timeout errors.
[00:00:50] Jordan: Got it. On the Dedicated plan we can provision reserved GPU pools to remove queueing — that's what we were thinking for the upgrade.
[00:00:56] Liam: Question on regions — we want EU and AP for latency and data residency. Does Redwood support eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 as dedicated regions?
[00:01:05] Maya: Yes we do support those regions; for Dedicated we can allocate dedicated pools in those regions but it requires lead time for capacity allocation and a small regional surcharge. We suggest staged rollouts — start us-west-2 sandbox then add eu, then ap to validate.
[00:01:20] Priya: Staged sounds fine, timeline is tight though — our renewal is end of month so we need to know cost impact and lead times.
[00:01:28] Jordan: Understood. For an 18-month commit we can offer a deeper discount — 12 vs 18 months makes a decent difference. We'll capture options in the updated proposal.
[00:01:36] Diego: Also wanted to confirm encryption key handling. We need KMS integration and HSM for certain data sets.
[00:01:42] Maya: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations in Private deployments and Dedicated with BYOK. There are some network config items for VPC peering and cross-region routing.
[00:01:54] Liam: Cool. One thing — last time there were a few misattributed logs and it took time to trace. Audit logs and tracing are big for us.
[00:02:02] Jordan: We can include extended audit log retention as part of the enterprise add-on, and show you the console traces. We'll send sample logs and the tracing deck.
[00:02:10] Sofia: From procurement perspective we need SOC 2 and ISO certs, and a copy of the network diagram. Also need to understand SLA credits and uptime numbers.
[00:02:18] Jordan: Yes — SOC 2 and ISO are available, we'll share artifacts and the network diagram. SLA is 99.9% for Dedicated with credits per the contract.
[00:02:27] Priya: On perf — can you walk through the benchmark plan? We want to simulate peak Black Friday-ish load.
[00:02:34] Maya: Plan is to provision a sandbox in us-west-2 with same model variant and quantization we run in prod, run ramp tests to two different RPS curves, measure p50/p95/p99 and token/sec, and exercise KV cache hit patterns. We'll upload results and an annotated spreadsheet.
[00:02:53] Diego: Will the KV cache be shared across regions or separate? We have cross-region sessions and want low-latency reads.
[00:02:59] Maya: Typically KV cache is per-region for latency reasons; we can set up cross-region replication for session continuity but there's added cost. We'll document tradeoffs.
[00:03:10] Liam: Are there any gotchas with model variants? We rely on a mix of open models and some custom-tuned weights. We can't have unpredictable regressions when switching.
[00:03:18] Jordan: We recommend pinning model versions and using rollout policies — Redwood Optimize will flag quality regressions against your eval set. We'll include model pinning steps in ops doc.
[00:03:28] Priya: Good. Cost question: if we go dedicated with two extra regions, what's the expected delta? Ballpark numbers help us.
[00:03:36] Jordan: Ballpark — adding a dedicated pool in a region is roughly X% of your current committed spend per region; for an 18-month commit with reserved capacity we can show two pricing tiers. I'll put exact numbers in the updated quote.
[00:03:48] Sofia: We'll need the quote and SOW to start procurement. Our usual cycle is about two weeks for PO once pricing is agreed.
[00:03:55] Jordan: Great — target to get you a proposal with pricing and region details by Tue 2027-03-15.
[00:04:02] Liam: Quick follow — any vendor lock concerns if we need to shift models or run on-prem?
[00:04:08] Maya: For Private deployments we offer on-prem or VPC modes; the control plane can be customer-managed. There's some engineering lift but it's supported.
[00:04:16] Diego: For the sandbox, what model size and quantization do you suggest? We typically use a 13B variant with 8-bit quantization for cost-performance.
[00:04:24] Maya: 13B with 8-bit is a common sweet spot. We'll mirror that in the sandbox and also test a 7B to compare cost/latency.
[00:04:32] Jordan: Any competitor pushback from your side? Are you evaluating others seriously?
[00:04:36] Liam: We have RFP responses from Anthropic and a proof-of-concept with Bedrock; Replicate was used for some experiments. The differentiators for you are observability and the cost controls.
[00:04:46] Jordan: Understood. We'll highlight our per-route cost breakdown and batching/caching savings in the proposal.
[00:04:52] Priya: One more: can we get an SLA playbook in case the dedicated pool gets overloaded and fails over to hosted models? We prefer automatic fallback.
[00:05:00] Maya: Yes — we can configure smart routing and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in another region or to hosted capacity. We'll share example policies.
[00:05:09] Sofia: Procurement question — for an 18-month extension do you need a signature on the master services agreement or a PO first?
[00:05:15] Jordan: Either works; typically a signed MSA plus a PO is ideal. We'll send the MSA and a redlined copy for you.
[00:05:22] Priya: Thanks. Anything else from Redwood?
[00:05:26] Maya: We'll include the perf test plan in the sandbox invite and a link to the benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:05:32] Jordan: Ok, recap — Jordan sends updated proposal and security artifacts by 2027-03-15. Maya provisions sandbox and runs perf tests, results by 2027-03-16. Priya confirms budget by 2027-03-18. Sofia shares procurement contact and redlines by 2027-03-17.
[00:05:45] Liam: Sounds good, thanks all.
[00:05:48] Sofia: Thanks.
[00:05:50] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links.
[00:05:55] END OF TRANSCRIPT

References: Deck links and benchmark spreadsheet were mentioned — e.g., https://redwood.example.com/decks/newcrest-renewal and https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/newcrest-blackfriday.csv (placeholders).
